_meta.description: Authoritative governance contract defining which actions the ORBIT agent may execute autonomously, under what conditions, and at what audit level. All numeric thresholds are resolved by name against thresholds.json at runtime. This file owns rules; thresholds.json owns numbers.

actions.description: Merge semantically identical or near-duplicate notifications into a single grouped entry to reduce noise.
Discard a low-confidence or spam notification without surfacing it to the user.
Create a new local reminder derived from extracted commitment text (notification, OCR, or audio).
Update mutable fields (title, description, notes) of an existing local task without changing its schedule.
Adjust the priority tier (P0/P1/P2) of an existing local task based on new context signals.
Reorder or re-categorize multiple tasks in bulk following a significant context shift.
Move an existing local reminder to a new timestamp derived from updated commitment evidence.
Escalate or de-escalate a task priority tier in response to converging high-confidence evidence.
Permanently remove a task, note, or stored evidence record from local storage. Irreversible.
Adjust the timestamp of a locally managed calendar reminder in response to deadline evidence.
Cancel a scheduled calendar event. May affect external participants; cannot be undone automatically.
Confirm attendance, agree to a deadline, or otherwise commit on behalf of the user to an external party.
Dispatch an outbound message (quick reply or composed reply) to an external contact via a messaging app.
Persist a structured context record derived from any sensory input to local in-memory or SQLite state.
Update the agent's internal representation of user goals, current focus, or active commitments.
Persist a structured context record derived from a CameraX OCR frame to local state.
Extract a commitment or deadline from OCR-recognized text and create a corresponding local reminder.

conflict_policy.description: When contradictory evidence exists for the same entity the effective tier is unconditionally escalated to SENSITIVE, regardless of the action's default_tier. The existing value is preserved until the user explicitly resolves the conflict. Silent overwrites are never permitted.

escalation_policy.description: Rules governing when and how a pending decision is forwarded to the laptop deep-reasoning layer via Office Kit. A pending action must be held, never executed, while escalation is in flight. A laptop result may raise the effective tier but never lower it.

evidence_policy.description: Staleness rules. Evidence older than max_age_key (resolved in thresholds.json) is considered stale. A stale-evidence-backed action is demoted one autonomy tier: REVERSIBLE becomes SENSITIVE. SAFE is the floor and does not demote further.

privacy_policy.description: Local-first defaults. Raw event payloads never leave the device. Only structured context fields are permitted to cross the Office Kit bridge to the laptop layer.

LOW_BATTERY_POLICY.description: When battery falls below the threshold, local inference is throttled, escalation to the laptop is suspended, and SENSITIVE actions are held rather than prompted until the device is charging.

OFFLINE_POLICY.description: When network connectivity is unavailable the phone must continue functioning fully standalone. Local inference runs unthrottled. Office Kit escalation is disabled; outbound bridge messages are buffered locally and flushed automatically on reconnect. SENSITIVE actions requiring escalation are held.

global_defaults.description: Fail-closed defaults. Any action or domain not matched by this file resolves to SENSITIVE, requiring explicit user confirmation before execution.
